name: Setúbal
title: Setúbal Ship Thickness Gauging | Car Carriers & Bulkers
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Setúbal on the Sado estuary: car carriers, bulk carriers, pulp and cement ships, gauged alongside and at the anchorage.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Cargo Ships on the Sado Estuary at Setúbal
intro: Setúbal is a cargo port on the Sado estuary, south of the Tagus, serving a car plant, a pulp and paper mill, cement works and a steady flow of dry bulk. Ships come and go on the tide through a dredged channel and some lie at the berth for days. That gives time for gauging alongside, between cargo operations. Atlantis NDT brings a technician team from India to the ship in the estuary and reports for the superintendent.

highlights.p: Vehicle carriers load cars built in the region at the ro-ro terminal. With decks clear after discharge and before loading, the team can gauge deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks.

highlights.h: Hold gauging after pulp and bulk
highlights.p: Pulp, paper and dry bulk ships empty their holds at the quay. Frames, lower hopper plating and hatch coamings become accessible once the holds are swept, so hold gauging can follow discharge directly.

highlights.h: Estuary calls timed to the tide
highlights.p: Deep-draught ships use the channel at the favourable state of tide. We plan the arrival and the gauging around the pilot and berth times, with a fallback if the call slips.

port.h: A river port behind the Arrábida hills
p: Setúbal lies on the northern shore of the Sado estuary, with the Arrábida range behind it and the long Tróia peninsula across the water. Ships enter from the Atlantic through the estuary mouth and follow a dredged channel to terminals strung along the north bank. The estuary is also a nature reserve, home to a resident dolphin population, so shipping is managed carefully, and the channel imposes limits on draught and sometimes on timing.

The cargoes reflect the industry of the surrounding region. A vehicle plant inland sends cars to the ro-ro terminal for export on car carriers, a paper company ships pulp and paper through its own berths, and cement and clinker ships call at the Outão terminal. Dry bulk terminals receive grain, fertiliser and other bulk, and a ferry crosses to Tróia for passengers and vehicles. Compared with the Tagus, the traffic is more industrial and less tied to cruise or container flows, and it moves in a steady pattern.

Ships anchor in the estuary or just off its mouth while they wait for the tide or a berth. Atlantic swell stops at the bar, and inside the estuary the water is sheltered, so launch-served work at anchor is more practical than at many open-coast ports. Winter southwesterly gales occasionally close the entrance, and fog in cold months can delay pilotage. For gauging the main variables are tide and berth availability, rather than weather inside the estuary itself.

facilities.h: Berths, anchorage and the yard across the water
p: Most gauging at Setúbal happens alongside at the cargo terminals. The ro-ro berth suits car carriers between discharge and loading, the pulp and paper berths allow hold work once the cargo is out, and the bulk quays serve ships that have discharged grain or fertiliser. Cement ships lie at their own terminal, where dust control and the shipper's rules shape the access. In each case the superintendent confirms the cargo programme with the agent, and the team plans the work to follow discharge.

Setúbal also has a large ship repair yard on the estuary, where tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers are docked, and it is a short run from the commercial berths. Ships that need a docking can move there, and our team can follow with equipment and permits in place. For ships waiting at anchor, the sheltered estuary allows boarding by launch to carry out pre-docking or condition work, provided the harbour master clears the transfer and sea conditions are suitable.
list: Ro-ro terminal for vehicles: car-deck, ramp and ballast-tank gauging on car carriers between discharge and loading.
Pulp and paper berths: hold frames, hatch coamings and ballast tanks on forest-products ships after discharge.
Cement and clinker terminal: hold and deck gauging on cement carriers, under the terminal's dust and access rules.
Dry bulk quays: hold, hopper tank and hatch cover readings on bulk carriers once the cargo is out.
Estuary anchorage: launch-served pre-docking and condition gauging on ships waiting for a berth or the tide.
Repair yard on the estuary: gauging during docking, for ships moving there from the commercial berths.

context.h: Portuguese maritime authority and EU requirements
p: Portuguese ports are inspected under the Paris MoU, and the national maritime authority and the directorate-general for maritime resources oversee flag and port state matters. Foreign-flag ships calling at Setúbal can be selected for port state control inspections like any other Paris MoU port, and structural condition is one of the areas inspectors look at. A current thickness record helps a master or superintendent answer questions about corrosion without delaying the ship.

EU regulations affect these ships in several ways. The Ship Recycling Regulation requires a valid Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and owners of older bulk carriers and car carriers often update it when planning a sale. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime also bear on ships trading to and from Portugal. Car carriers on European routes are a particular case, since newer vessels are LNG dual-fuel, and owners of older tonnage want to know whether the steel will last through the transition.

jobs.p: Work at Setúbal follows cargo operations. The superintendent names the spaces to be measured, the agent confirms the discharge programme, and the team arrives when the holds or decks are clear. Where a docking is planned at the repair yard or elsewhere, the readings feed directly into the steel estimate. Typical requests are:
list: A car carrier between discharge and loading: gauging of lower-hold and fixed deck plating, plus magnetic particle testing at ramp and deck-support welds.
A forest-products ship after pulp discharge: hold frames, lower hopper plating and hatch coamings, with dye penetrant at doubler edges.
A bulk carrier after grain discharge: gauging of holds, topside and hopper tanks ahead of an intermediate or renewal survey.
A cement carrier at its terminal: deck, hatch cover and ballast-tank readings within the terminal's access arrangements.
Pre-purchase gauging on a vessel lying at anchor in the estuary while a buyer completes the inspection.

logistics: Lisbon Airport is the usual arrival point for international travellers, and the road south crosses the Tagus before reaching Setúbal, so the transfer needs a planned allowance for traffic. Technicians from India need a Schengen visa for Portugal, which we apply for once the ship's call is confirmed. Port and terminal access, ISPS clearance and any launch transfer are arranged through the ship's agent, who receives the team's passport and certificate details before arrival.

faqs.q: Can a car carrier be gauged at Setúbal between discharge and loading?
faqs.a: Yes, if the call gives enough time. With the decks clear, a team can cover a defined set of fixed deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks, and carry out crack detection at suspect welds. We agree the sequence beforehand so the highest-priority areas are measured first.

faqs.q: Does the tide affect when you can work?
faqs.a: It affects when ships arrive and leave, rather than the gauging itself. Deep-draught ships use the channel at favourable states of tide, so the call time is set by pilotage. We plan around the confirmed berth time and keep a fallback if the ship's arrival changes.

faqs.q: Can ships be gauged at anchor in the Sado estuary?
faqs.a: Yes, when the harbour master allows a launch transfer and conditions are calm. The estuary is more sheltered than the open coast, so anchorage jobs are practical. They are limited to spaces that the ship has ventilated and made safe, and the scope is smaller than at a berth.

faqs.q: Is hold gauging possible during cargo operations?
faqs.a: Only in holds that are empty and cleaned, and only where the ship and terminal allow it. On pulp and bulk ships the practical window is after discharge, before the next loading. We confirm with the agent which holds will be free and for how long.

faqs.q: Where do Setúbal ships go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: Often to the repair yard on the same estuary, a short move from the commercial berths. Others go to yards elsewhere in Portugal, Spain or the Mediterranean. Readings from Setúbal use TM plan references, so any yard and class surveyor can use them.
